rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MAGNA CARTA OF AGRICULTURAL OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES
rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is unfortunate that the career path of agricultural officers has been broken - limiting their chances to venture into higher positions and/or other offices of regional and national scope. Because the said position is onloy optional, local executives may opt not to create the position or appoint/assign someone as agricultural officer. Despite this status, the office of the agricultural officer is especially to perform its devolved functions in attaining its goal of teaching/asssiting the farmers on modern farm technology to uplift their living conditions. Defines the terms " AGRICULTURAL OFFICER" and "AGRICULTURAL EMPLOYEE" as used in this Act. Shall cover all eligible agricultural officers and employees, as well as all agriicultural practitioners in the government or nongovernment service. Provides for these concerns: (1) recruitment and qualifications; (2) performance instruction and merit promotion; (3) security of tenure; (4) safeguards in administrative proceedings

rows.abstract: Rationale: The national government is privileged with an exemption from the payment of postage for official mails to expedite the conduct of official business. Such privilege however is denied the local governments whose activities have increased significantly because of an expanded mandate. Provides, therefore, for the following --- "SEC. 3 Franking Privilege shall hereby be granted to local governments, provided, that such privilege shall only be used in the conduct of official business and,provided further, that such privilege shall not be used for personal or partisan political purposes." rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING THE SCOPE OF 'NATIONAL PATRIMONY' AND AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE ARTICLE 421 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 346, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE CIVIL CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Defines the scope of "NATIONAL PATRIMONY" (Art. 421 of the Civil Code of the Philippines) with this amendatory provision: > Article 421. All other property of the State, which is not of the character stated in the preceding article, is patrimonial property. > HOWEVER, WITHOUT PREJUDICE TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE 1987 PHILIPPINE CONSTITUTION, WHEN REFERRING TO NATIONAL PATRIMONY, IT SHALL MEAN FILIPINO CULTURAL HERITAGE AND TREASURES. PROVIDED, THAT: CULTURAL HERITAGE AND TREASURES SHALL INCLUDE AND EMBRACE: (1) HISTORICAL LANDMARKS; (2) ANCESTRAL HOUSES; (3) MONUMENTS; (4) NATIONAL SHRINES; (5) RESIDENCE OF LATE PHILIPPINE PRESIDENTS; (6) MEMORABILIA AND RELICS OF LATE FILIPINO PERSONALITIES; AND (7) ANY PROPERTY, TANGIBLE OR INTANGIBLE, WHIICH IS CHARACTERIZED BY FILIPINO INGENUITY, TAINTED WITH HISTORICAL VALUE AND SIGNIFICANCE, IMPRESSED WITH NATIONAL INTEREST AND REFLECTIVE OF THE FILIPINO SOUL.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1997-03-05

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 61 AND 103 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 856, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'CODE OF SANITATION'
rows.abstract: Seeks to REGULATE the maintenance of massage clinics and suana bath establishments to provide more STRINGENT penalties for the violations thereof. Prescribes the following regulatory requirements: (1) Every massage cubicle and sauna bath cubicle must be adequately ventilated and provided with sliding translucent curtains or transparent sliding glass doors without lock which will be seven feet height with a clearance of two (2) feet from the floor with a two feet space from below and one foot from above.  Each cubicle must also be equipped with a suitable and clean massage table. (2) The operation hours of massage and sauna baths is from twelve (12) in the morning to twelve (12) in the evening; and (3) No display window for the masseurs, maassage clinic attendants and sauna bath attendants shall be provided.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 1997-03-05

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A COMPREHENSIVE FACULTY ASSISTANCE AND DEVELOPMENT FUND FOR THE PURPOSE OF GIVING GOVERNMENT SUBSIDY TO ALL PRIVATE SCHOOLS IN THE FORM OF ALLOWANCES, AND AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE, SECTION 13 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6728, OTHERWISEKNOWN AS 'AN ACT PROVIDING GOVERNMENT ASSISTANCE TO STUDENTS AND TEACHERS IN PRIVATE EDUCATION (GASTPE), AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Under Ra 6728, otherwise known as The Salary Standardization Law, public school teachers receive a minimum salary of Eight Thousand Six Hundred Pesos (P8,600.00) while private school teachers in the provinces receive a meager amount ranging from Two Thousand Five Hundered to Three Thousand Pesos (P2,500.00) - (P3,000.00) per month which results to a great imbalance of salaries between public and private school teachers.  As a consequence, this only results to total dismay of school teachers from private schools who cannot be accommodated at teaching posts in the public schools. Moreover, it will finally end up in the closure of private schools in the provinces. Seeks, therefore, to amend Sec. 13 of Ra 6728 by granting GOVERNMENTT SUBSIDY in the from of allowances to all private school teachers in orderr to elimiante inequities in salary.
rows.status: Substituted by HB10462

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS PENSION FUND AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Creating a pension fund for retired Filipino overseas workers is in accordance with the protection to labor clause of the Constitution. Under Section 18, Article II thereof, it states that "the State affirms labor as a primary social economic force.  It shall protect the rights of workers and promote their welfare." Hences approval of this bill is highly recommended. "Overseas Filipino Workers Pension Fund Act of 1997" applies to all overseas Filipino contract workers who are duly registered with the POEA and the Commission on Filipino Overseas (CFO). Mandates the same to remit FIVE PERCENT (5%) of their gross monthly income to the Fund for five (5) years.
